native_mechanisms: A stone on a corner finalizes that place's distance, never reconsidered (permanently settled set).
A duck carries a spooled thread whose length is the running sum of road lengths to reach it (tentative distance label built by adding edge weight to the source's settled length).

Each round, find the leader duck with the shortest carried thread among the unstoned and settle it before any other duck moves (repeated global minimum selection over unsettled labels), re-tracing every shot to its landing before trusting it.
Roads toward houses with no far side (out-degree-zero targets) are left slack, thrown away unspooled, and never measured again.
Corners no duck ever reaches stay bare — unreachable distance left as unattained/lost.
core_technique: Dijkstra's algorithm on a CSR graph with a work-estimate switch between an O(n^2) SIMD (AVX2) two-pass linear argmin scan over tentative distances (dense case, dead-end vertices permuted out of the scanned prefix) and a lazy 4-ary binary-heap Dijkstra (sparse case).
